fields.sourceAttribution: System Design for PM — original course content.
fields.domains/0/keyQuestion: Where does product data live and what makes it hard to change?
fields.domains/1/keyQuestion: How do system components negotiate and why do they break?
fields.domains/2/keyQuestion: What happens when there are 100 times more users?
fields.domains/3/keyQuestion: How much does a second of waiting cost, and how much for a single request?
fields.domains/4/keyQuestion: What makes up an AI feature and why does its cost grow faster than its scale?
fields.domains/5/keyQuestion: Who sees what and what must we be able to delete?
fields.blocks/0/nodes/0/keyQuestion: what objects make up the product and how are they connected?
fields.blocks/0/nodes/0/pmDecision: read the data schema and understand which features it enables and which it makes expensive.
fields.blocks/0/nodes/1/keyQuestion: where exactly does data live and why does an engineer say “that's not our database”?
fields.blocks/0/nodes/1/pmDecision: understand why some data is fetched instantly while other data requires a whole project.
fields.blocks/0/nodes/2/keyQuestion: why does “adding one field” take an hour sometimes and two weeks other times?
fields.blocks/0/nodes/2/pmDecision: estimate the cost of changing the data model before promising a feature.
fields.blocks/0/nodes/3/keyQuestion: why is searching by one field instant, but not by another?
fields.blocks/0/nodes/3/pmDecision: understand why a filter that seems “easy to add” requires work, and which filter is actually cheap.
fields.blocks/0/nodes/4/keyQuestion: which data must always be consistent, and which can drift apart?
fields.blocks/0/nodes/4/pmDecision: distinguish operations where errors are unacceptable from those where they are fine, avoiding paying for guarantees where they aren't needed.
fields.blocks/1/nodes/0/keyQuestion: when is data duplication a mistake, and when is it a solution?
fields.blocks/1/nodes/0/pmDecision: understand what price you pay for a fast screen, and knowingly agree to pay it.
fields.blocks/1/nodes/1/keyQuestion: how many indexes can a table afford?
fields.blocks/1/nodes/1/pmDecision: understand that every new filter in the UI is a negotiation, not just a request.
fields.blocks/1/nodes/2/keyQuestion: what will the user see one second after taking an action?
fields.blocks/1/nodes/2/pmDecision: design the UI so that data latency does not look like a product error.
fields.blocks/1/nodes/3/keyQuestion: why do numbers in the product and on the dashboard disagree?
fields.blocks/1/nodes/3/pmDecision: know which number to trust in which context, and avoid demanding impossible freshness.
fields.blocks/1/nodes/4/keyQuestion: what happens when data no longer fits into a single database?
fields.blocks/1/nodes/4/pmDecision: spot the limit early and participate in a choice that cannot be easily reversed later.
fields.blocks/1/nodes/5/keyQuestion: how long does data live and what happens when it is deleted?
fields.blocks/1/nodes/5/pmDecision: promise the user only what the product technically delivers.
fields.blocks/2/nodes/0/keyQuestion: which data decisions will determine product capabilities for years to come?
fields.blocks/2/nodes/0/pmDecision: distinguish reversible decisions from irreversible ones, and spend discussion time on the latter.
fields.blocks/2/nodes/1/keyQuestion: how do you change the data model of a live product without downtime?
fields.blocks/2/nodes/1/pmDecision: properly plan data changes in the roadmap as multiple releases, not as a single task.
fields.blocks/2/nodes/2/keyQuestion: how does the system serve multiple enterprise clients, and what can it promise them?
fields.blocks/2/nodes/2/pmDecision: know what isolation and residency guarantees the product can offer in enterprise deals.
fields.blocks/2/nodes/3/title: Source of truth and data lineage
fields.blocks/2/nodes/3/keyQuestion: why does data on a single customer live across five systems, and which one to trust?
fields.blocks/2/nodes/3/pmDecision: assign an owner and source of truth for every entity to end disputes over numbers.
fields.blocks/2/nodes/4/keyQuestion: what must be written about data so the engineering team doesn't reject the spec?
fields.blocks/2/nodes/4/pmDecision: write a section that resolves questions before backlog grooming, not after.
fields.blocks/3/title: How system components talk to each other
fields.blocks/3/nodes/0/keyQuestion: what happens between a click and the result?
fields.blocks/3/nodes/0/pmDecision: understand where a business rule lives, because that dictates how fast you can change it.
fields.blocks/3/nodes/1/title: What an API is and how to read it
fields.blocks/3/nodes/1/keyQuestion: how systems agree on what can be requested and what response to expect?
fields.blocks/3/nodes/1/pmDecision: read a third-party API and tell which features are possible on top of it and which are not.
fields.blocks/3/nodes/2/keyQuestion: what do the server response numbers mean, and what should be shown to the user?
fields.blocks/3/nodes/2/pmDecision: design product behavior for each error class instead of showing a generic error message.
fields.blocks/3/nodes/3/keyQuestion: why does one action happen instantly while another shows “processing”?
fields.blocks/3/nodes/3/pmDecision: design honest wait states instead of an infinite spinner.
fields.blocks/3/nodes/4/keyQuestion: what happens to the product when a third-party system goes down?
fields.blocks/3/nodes/4/pmDecision: decide in advance how the product operates without each of its dependencies.
fields.blocks/4/nodes/0/keyQuestion: how do API styles differ from a product perspective, rather than syntax?
fields.blocks/4/nodes/0/pmDecision: understand why the same screen in one product takes a single request, while in another it takes six.
fields.blocks/4/nodes/1/keyQuestion: why can't you simply rename a field after release?
fields.blocks/4/nodes/1/pmDecision: plan contract changes as a process with a migration window, not as a quick fix.
fields.blocks/4/nodes/2/keyQuestion: which operations are safe to retry, and how to make any operation safe?
fields.blocks/4/nodes/2/pmDecision: determine where retries are acceptable and where they cause duplicate financial transactions.
fields.blocks/4/nodes/3/keyQuestion: what does an “accepted” response mean, and when will the job actually complete?
fields.blocks/4/nodes/3/pmDecision: understand delivery guarantees provided by the system and design the product around them.
fields.blocks/4/nodes/4/keyQuestion: how do you know that something happened in an external system?
fields.blocks/4/nodes/4/pmDecision: choose between real-time awareness and operational simplicity, knowing the cost of both.
fields.blocks/4/nodes/5/keyQuestion: how many requests are allowed and what happens when you exceed the limit?
fields.blocks/4/nodes/5/pmDecision: turn rate limiting from technical protection into a deliberate product and business decision.
fields.blocks/5/nodes/0/keyQuestion: who is the API user and what do they pay for?
fields.blocks/5/nodes/0/pmDecision: decide whether to open up the platform, understanding the long-term commitment it creates.
fields.blocks/5/nodes/1/keyQuestion: what changes in the product when components react to events instead of calling each other directly?
fields.blocks/5/nodes/1/pmDecision: understand why adding features became easier while debugging issues got harder.
fields.blocks/5/nodes/2/keyQuestion: what does architecture choice mean for product delivery speed?
fields.blocks/5/nodes/2/pmDecision: take part in drawing service boundaries, because they will become product boundaries.
fields.blocks/5/nodes/3/keyQuestion: what did we promise forever without even realizing it?
fields.blocks/5/nodes/3/pmDecision: realize which part of the contract becomes a guarantee, and limit it intentionally.
fields.blocks/5/nodes/4/keyQuestion: what does the customer's security team ask, and why must you know the answers in advance?
fields.blocks/5/nodes/4/pmDecision: turn the client's security questionnaire from a barrier into a part of the product.
fields.blocks/6/nodes/0/keyQuestion: what does “one hundred thousand users” mean in terms the system understands?
fields.blocks/6/nodes/0/pmDecision: translate product plans into load and know when a plan requires advance preparation.
fields.blocks/6/nodes/1/keyQuestion: what does “adding capacity” mean, and why doesn't it always work?
fields.blocks/6/nodes/1/pmDecision: understand whether the product's growth has a technical ceiling and where it lies.
fields.blocks/6/nodes/2/keyQuestion: where on the diagram is the spot whose failure stops everything?
fields.blocks/6/nodes/2/pmDecision: know which failures take down the entire product and decide how to handle them.
fields.blocks/6/nodes/3/keyQuestion: why does the user sometimes see stale data, and what do we gain from it?
fields.blocks/6/nodes/3/pmDecision: decide where showing slightly stale data is acceptable for speed, and where it is not.
fields.blocks/6/nodes/4/keyQuestion: what to show when part of the system is down?
fields.blocks/6/nodes/4/pmDecision: design a degraded mode in advance for every key scenario.
fields.blocks/7/nodes/0/keyQuestion: what exactly are we promising and how do we measure it?
fields.blocks/7/nodes/0/pmDecision: derive the reliability target from user behavior rather than accepting it as a technical constant.
fields.blocks/7/nodes/1/keyQuestion: how much does each additional nine cost?
fields.blocks/7/nodes/1/pmDecision: avoid promising reliability that requires architectural overhead if the user doesn't need it.
fields.blocks/7/nodes/2/keyQuestion: how does the system survive a neighboring service outage without worsening it?
fields.blocks/7/nodes/2/pmDecision: understand why naive retries turn a slowdown into a full outage.
fields.blocks/7/nodes/3/keyQuestion: how does the system adapt to changing load?
fields.blocks/7/nodes/3/pmDecision: know how fast the system responds to traffic spikes and plan events accordingly.
fields.blocks/7/nodes/4/keyQuestion: what to do when incoming work exceeds what the system can process?
fields.blocks/7/nodes/4/pmDecision: decide which requests get prioritized when capacity falls short.
fields.blocks/7/nodes/5/keyQuestion: what is the product manager's role during an outage?
fields.blocks/7/nodes/5/pmDecision: own communication and product decisions during an incident without getting in the way of technical recovery.
fields.blocks/8/nodes/0/keyQuestion: how much reliability does this product need, and where do you learn that?
fields.blocks/8/nodes/0/pmDecision: derive the reliability target from user behavior instead of adopting an industry baseline.
fields.blocks/8/nodes/1/keyQuestion: what do we do if data is lost or a site is unavailable?
fields.blocks/8/nodes/1/pmDecision: specify how much data loss is acceptable and how fast recovery must happen.
fields.blocks/8/nodes/2/keyQuestion: when are multiple regions needed, and what does it cost?
fields.blocks/8/nodes/2/pmDecision: distinguish reliability-driven requirements from geographic or compliance requirements.
fields.blocks/8/nodes/3/keyQuestion: how to make sure the system will handle what we planned?
fields.blocks/8/nodes/3/pmDecision: translate product plans into capacity requirements before launch, not after.
fields.blocks/8/nodes/4/keyQuestion: how to verify that disaster recovery plans actually work?
fields.blocks/8/nodes/4/pmDecision: make regular testing of contingency plans a standard practice rather than an experiment.
fields.blocks/9/nodes/0/pmDecision: label the problem accurately, because the remedies are different.
fields.blocks/9/nodes/1/keyQuestion: why does “average response time of 200 ms” tell you nothing about the product?
fields.blocks/9/nodes/1/pmDecision: look at the distribution rather than averages, and understand how many users are in the long tail.
fields.blocks/9/nodes/2/keyQuestion: where exactly is time spent between a click and the result?
fields.blocks/9/nodes/2/pmDecision: isolate the bottleneck before talking to the team, so you discuss solutions instead of hunting for the bug.
fields.blocks/9/nodes/3/keyQuestion: is the app slow or is it the server?
fields.blocks/9/nodes/3/pmDecision: route complaints to where the problem actually lies, not where you usually look.
fields.blocks/9/nodes/4/keyQuestion: why is performance terrible for some users while metrics look good?
fields.blocks/9/nodes/4/pmDecision: know what share of your audience experiences performance different from the median.
fields.blocks/10/nodes/0/keyQuestion: how do you break down a 1.5-second target across components?
fields.blocks/10/nodes/0/pmDecision: turn latency goals into concrete constraints for each system component.
fields.blocks/10/nodes/1/title: Where to look for time savings
fields.blocks/10/nodes/1/keyQuestion: what should be sped up to make a meaningful difference?
fields.blocks/10/nodes/1/pmDecision: avoid spending weeks of team effort on a component that yields a three percent gain.
fields.blocks/10/nodes/2/keyQuestion: can you shorten the physical distance to the user?
fields.blocks/10/nodes/2/pmDecision: understand what can be moved closer cheaply and what requires a different architecture.
fields.blocks/10/nodes/3/keyQuestion: how to tell in five minutes if a plan is realistic?
fields.blocks/10/nodes/3/pmDecision: verify order-of-magnitude feasibility on your own without waiting for team estimates.
fields.blocks/10/nodes/4/keyQuestion: how much does one request, one user, or one order cost?
fields.blocks/10/nodes/4/pmDecision: know the infrastructure cost of product decisions, not just engineering effort.
fields.blocks/10/nodes/5/keyQuestion: how to tell if an optimization isn't worth the work?
fields.blocks/10/nodes/5/pmDecision: distinguish a real performance problem from engineering perfectionism.
fields.blocks/11/nodes/0/pmDecision: forecast expenses based on product roadmap rather than reacting to cloud bills.
fields.blocks/11/nodes/1/keyQuestion: which architectural decisions define unit economics?
fields.blocks/11/nodes/1/pmDecision: see which technical choices make the product profitable or unprofitable at scale.
fields.blocks/11/nodes/2/pmDecision: calculate total cost of ownership instead of comparing subscription price to initial build time.
fields.blocks/11/nodes/3/keyQuestion: how to justify refactoring in business terms?
fields.blocks/11/nodes/3/pmDecision: translate tech debt into concrete line-item overpayments in the plan.
fields.blocks/11/nodes/4/keyQuestion: what to specify so performance doesn't degrade quietly?
fields.blocks/11/nodes/4/pmDecision: make performance a verifiable acceptance criterion, not a wish.
fields.blocks/12/nodes/0/keyQuestion: what happens when a product “queries the model”?
fields.blocks/12/nodes/0/pmDecision: speak the same language with engineers and understand what drives response cost and quality.
fields.blocks/12/nodes/1/keyQuestion: what happens on every request, and what happened once?
fields.blocks/12/nodes/1/pmDecision: understand why the model doesn't know about yesterday's product changes and how to address it.
fields.blocks/12/nodes/2/keyQuestion: why do identical requests produce different answers?
fields.blocks/12/nodes/2/pmDecision: design a product where response variability doesn't look like a bug.
fields.blocks/12/nodes/3/keyQuestion: how much can a model see at once, and what happens when it doesn't fit?
fields.blocks/12/nodes/3/pmDecision: decide what goes into context when everything doesn't fit.
fields.blocks/12/nodes/4/keyQuestion: why do AI interfaces look the way they do?
fields.blocks/12/nodes/4/pmDecision: design waiting times around generation mechanics, not despite them.
fields.blocks/13/nodes/0/keyQuestion: how to give the model product knowledge if fine-tuning isn't suitable?
fields.blocks/13/nodes/0/pmDecision: understand what RAG consists of and where it breaks, because it usually breaks outside the model.
fields.blocks/13/nodes/1/pmDecision: understand what vector search can and cannot do to avoid promising the impossible.
fields.blocks/13/nodes/2/keyQuestion: how much does an AI feature cost, and how do you keep it in check?
fields.blocks/13/nodes/2/pmDecision: calculate the unit cost of an AI feature before launch and know the levers to lower it.
fields.blocks/13/nodes/3/keyQuestion: how to measure if an AI feature works well?
fields.blocks/13/nodes/3/pmDecision: build measurable quality, without which you can neither improve nor swap out the model.
fields.blocks/13/nodes/4/keyQuestion: how to stop the model from saying things it shouldn't?
fields.blocks/13/nodes/4/pmDecision: constrain behavior with product controls rather than relying on hope in the model.
fields.blocks/13/nodes/5/keyQuestion: what changes when a model acts instead of just answering?
fields.blocks/13/nodes/5/pmDecision: decide which actions the model can perform autonomously and which require human approval.
fields.blocks/14/nodes/0/keyQuestion: which model should solve the task?
fields.blocks/14/nodes/0/pmDecision: choose a model as a product trade-off, not a technical constant.
fields.blocks/14/nodes/1/keyQuestion: what does the product do when the model is unavailable, expensive, or failing?
fields.blocks/14/nodes/1/pmDecision: design AI feature fallback behavior just like for any external dependency.
fields.blocks/14/nodes/2/keyQuestion: when does it make sense to run the model yourself?
fields.blocks/14/nodes/2/pmDecision: understand under what conditions the unit economics flip, and don't do it before then.
fields.blocks/14/nodes/3/keyQuestion: what happens to data sent to the model?
fields.blocks/14/nodes/3/pmDecision: know and be able to explain where user data goes and what it is used for.
fields.blocks/14/nodes/4/keyQuestion: what to write so that an AI feature can be accepted?
fields.blocks/14/nodes/4/pmDecision: make AI feature quality a verifiable definition of done.
fields.blocks/15/nodes/0/keyQuestion: how does the system know who logged in and what they are allowed to do?
fields.blocks/15/nodes/0/pmDecision: design login and permissions as user journeys, not as technical formalities.
fields.blocks/15/nodes/1/keyQuestion: what does encryption protect against, and what doesn't it?
fields.blocks/15/nodes/1/pmDecision: don't promise users what encryption cannot deliver.
fields.blocks/15/nodes/2/keyQuestion: what counts as personal data, and why is it broader than it seems?
fields.blocks/15/nodes/2/pmDecision: understand which product data requires special handling before starting to collect it.
fields.blocks/15/nodes/3/keyQuestion: how does data end up on the outside?
fields.blocks/15/nodes/3/pmDecision: understand typical pathways so you don't design a vulnerability yourself.
fields.blocks/15/nodes/4/keyQuestion: where do access keys live, and why are they not in the client?
fields.blocks/15/nodes/4/pmDecision: understand why certain architectural choices are impossible and refrain from suggesting them.
fields.blocks/16/nodes/0/keyQuestion: what to do when simple roles are no longer enough?
fields.blocks/16/nodes/0/pmDecision: choose an access model that covers real customer organization structures without turning into a complex builder tool.
fields.blocks/16/nodes/1/keyQuestion: can you find out who did what and who viewed what?
fields.blocks/16/nodes/1/pmDecision: design audit logging as a product feature, not just technical logs.
fields.blocks/16/nodes/2/keyQuestion: what data should you not collect?
fields.blocks/16/nodes/2/pmDecision: treat data collection as a liability, not an asset.
fields.blocks/16/nodes/3/keyQuestion: what technically happens during deletion, and what can you promise?
fields.blocks/16/nodes/3/pmDecision: make a deletion promise that the product can actually deliver on.
fields.blocks/16/nodes/4/keyQuestion: who do we share user data with, and what are we responsible for?
fields.blocks/16/nodes/4/pmDecision: know the full list of data recipients and be ready to present it.
fields.blocks/16/nodes/5/keyQuestion: what can and cannot be sent to the model?
fields.blocks/16/nodes/5/pmDecision: set a rule before the team starts adding data to the prompt.
fields.blocks/17/nodes/0/keyQuestion: what do regulatory requirements change in product architecture?
fields.blocks/17/nodes/0/pmDecision: translate legal requirements into product and architectural ones rather than treating them as mere documents.
fields.blocks/17/nodes/1/keyQuestion: how to systematically find what could go wrong?
fields.blocks/17/nodes/1/pmDecision: conduct threat analysis for new features before implementation, not after an incident.
fields.blocks/17/nodes/2/keyQuestion: when should security be involved in development?
fields.blocks/17/nodes/2/pmDecision: embed security reviews into discovery to avoid getting blocked right before release.
fields.blocks/17/nodes/3/keyQuestion: what to write so that a feature doesn't cause problems?
fields.blocks/17/nodes/3/pmDecision: document data decisions so they can be verified.
fields.blocks/17/nodes/4/keyQuestion: when is formal certification needed, and what does it provide?
fields.blocks/17/nodes/4/pmDecision: decide if certification pays off for your segment and understand what it costs.
